data.name: Imam
data.gender_notes: Imam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'A-M-M' meaning 'to listen and to follow'. In Islamic tradition, an imam is a spiritual leader and guide for a Muslim community. The name Imam carries the meaning “Leader, Spiritual Guide” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Imam usually hope their child will grow to embody leader, spiritual guide and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A person who leads others in prayer and worship.
data.etymology: Imam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Leader, Spiritual Guide.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imam total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: إمام
in_arabic.meaning: قائد و پیشوا، مرجع دین و دنیا میں
in_arabic.long_meaning: إمام سے مراد ہے وہ شخص جو لوگوں کی رہنمائی کرتا ہے، خاص طور پر دین کے معاملات میں، اور اسلامی قانون اور روایات کے مطابق زندگی گزارنے کے لیے ایک نمونہ پیش کرتا ہے۔

in_urdu.name: امام
in_urdu.long_meaning: امام ایک ایسا لقب ہے جو اسلامی دنیا میں ایک اعلیٰ روحانی اور علمی قابلیت کے حامل شخص کو دیا جاتا ہے، جو اسلامی علوم کا گہرا علم رکھتا ہے اور لوگوں کو دینی اور دنیوی امور میں رہنمائی کرنے کی صلاحیت رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: इमाम
in_hindi.long_meaning: इमाम शब्द का अर्थ है एक ऐसा व्यक्ति जो मुसलमानों का नेतृत्व करता है, विशेष रूप से धार्मिक मामलों में, और इस्लामी परंपराओं और कानूनों के अनुसार जीवन जीने के लिए एक आदर्श प्रस्तुत करता है।

in_pashto.name: امام
in_pashto.long_meaning: امام هغه څوک دی چې د خلکو مشري کوي، په ځانګړي ډول ديني چارو کې، او د اسلامي قانون او دودونو سره سم د ژوند کولو لپاره يوه بېلګه وړاندې کوي.

in_english.name: Imam
in_english.meaning: Leader, guide, and authority in Islamic tradition
in_english.long_meaning: Imam refers to a person who leads Muslims in prayer, particularly in a mosque, and serves as a spiritual guide and authority on Islamic law and traditions. The term originates from the Arabic root 'أمام' (imām), meaning 'in front of' or 'leader', signifying a person who leads others in a particular activity or serves as a model for them to follow.

pronunciation.urdu: امام کا تلفظ: اے ایم اے ایم

data.cultural_impact: The title 'Imam' is revered amongst Muslims, representing a person of great knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual understanding. Imams lead congregational prayers, provide interpretations of the Quran and Hadiths, help resolve community issues, and often work to promote peace and social justice.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, an Imam acts as a link between the physical world and the divine presence of God. They serve as spiritual guides, facilitating the deepening of faith and the application of Islamic teachings in daily life. The title Imam bestows a profound sense of responsibility to inspire and lead others in the righteous path towards God.
